text.p: Shipping group Holyman Ltd said on Wednesday it had reduced its 1997 calendar year net profit forecast to the range of A$11.5 million to A$13.5 million from a A$14 million to A$16 million range predicted on June 6.
The company posted a net profit of A$21.86 million in the 12 months to December 31, 1996.

Holyman cited below-expectations performance for its 67 percent owned U.K. division Holyman Sally as the reason for the downgrade, adding that half year profit to June 30 would be materially affected by Holyman Sally's results in that period.
Holyman Sally operates high speed and conventional ferry services between Ramsgate, England and Ostende, Belgium, and between Ramsgate and Dunkirk, France.
European ferry operations earn most of their revenues in the peak summer months which would be reflected in the second half results, the company said.
However, Holyman noted that excluding Holyman Sally, other units were performing in line with existing forecasts. The remainder of Holyman Sally is owned by Silja Oy Ab of Finland.
By 11.50 a.m. (0150 GMT), Holyman shares were 42 cents lower at A$2.70 on turnover of 58,210 shares.
